title: Muse AI Agent 0-Day Lets Local Malware Hijack Prompts and Steal Authentication Tokens
content_md: A newly released proof-of-concept (PoC) for an alleged zero-day vulnerability in Muse, an AI assistant application. The flaw could let malware already running under a user’s account redirect the app’s dictation traffic, intercept prompts, and potentially obtain authentication material. The issue, detailed in Wardle’s “not-a-mused” repository, centers on an undocumented Muse configuration setting named endo_voyager_dictation_endpoint . Muse AI Agent 0-Day The project README says an unprivileged local process can modify the setting, enabling an attacker to replace the intended dictation destination with infrastructure they control. The PoC demonstrates how a malicious local program could monitor Muse’s dictation activity and redirect dictated content after a user clicks the microphone button. Wardle said the technique can capture dictated audio or prompts, supply prompt-injection content to the application, and potentially steal Muse authentication material. This is not a remote, unauthenticated attack. The attacker must first gain code-execution capability as the current user, such as through a separate malware infection, trojanized application, or malicious download. The reported weakness does not independently provide initial access or operating-system privilege escalation. Its impact, however, could be substantial if Muse has access to sensitive accounts, data, browser sessions, APIs, or enterprise services.
